summary.whatChanges: Vitest now prints a yellow "Vitest" labeled warning to stderr when an inline project that omits an explicit `extends` option registers plugins already inherited from the declaring config file, suggesting removing the duplicates or setting `extends` explicitly. E2E tests cover the warning and its suppression cases.
behaviorChanges: Running Vitest with an inline project that re-declares a plugin already present in the parent config emits a new warning on stderr naming the duplicated plugin(s) and the declaring config file.
No warning is emitted when the project sets `extends: true` or `extends: false` explicitly.
No warning is emitted when the duplicate plugin count originates from the declaring config itself (parent already lists it twice).
risks: Detection is by plugin `name` only, so distinct plugins sharing a name (or legitimately intentional duplicates) can trigger false-positive warnings.
Warnings written to stderr may break user tooling or snapshot tests that assert empty stderr output.
Counting logic (count > 1 && parentCount > 0 && count > parentCount) may miss or misreport cases where a plugin legitimately appears multiple times in both configs.
